# Experiment Design: Chemical-Feedback-Driven Molecule Generation for Targeted Kinase Discovery

## 0. Scope statement
This is a design-only deliverable. No experiment has been executed; it specifies a reproducible, CPU-feasible study. Environment constraints (no network, no GPU, 224 CPUs, system Python) are respected throughout: all chemistry via RDKit + scikit-learn on precomputed descriptors.

## 1. Hypothesis and pre-registered decision criterion
**Hypothesis (one sentence):** Embedding a chemical-feedback loop that couples p-logP, QED, and a learned binding-affinity proxy into generation improves the chemical quality of generated molecules, reduces structural hallucinations, aligns outputs with the real-world (ChEMBL active) distribution, and preserves structural diversity — without over-generating ultra-long carbon chains.

**Pre-registered decision criterion (primary):** The feedback loop is judged to *improve generation* if, for the full-feedback arm (C3) versus the no-feedback baseline (C0), **all** of the following hold with p < 0.05 (Bonferroni-corrected across the 4 primary comparisons):
1. Distribution alignment improves: Fréchet distance on Mordred descriptors to the ChEMBL active reference **drops ≥ 10%** (relative), **and**
2. Property score improves: mean QED of valid molecules **rises ≥ 0.05** (absolute) **and** mean affinity-proxy pKd improves (lower ΔG) by a pre-set margin, **and**
3. Diversity is preserved: scaffold coverage (Bertz index over unique scaffolds) and distinct-3 fall by **< 10%** (relative) — i.e., no significant mode collapse.
Tier-1 hallucination rate must not increase significantly (guardrail). The secondary diversity claim (ultra-long chains) is evaluated descriptively + a non-inferiority test (see §7).

## 2. Targeted-discovery task framing
Scaffold/target-class-conditioned generation for a single, well-populated kinase. **Target: EGFR — ChEMBL target ID CHEMBL213** (epidermal growth factor receptor, erbb1). EGFR carries >10 k ChEMBL actives, satisfying the ≥10k requirement. *Reproducibility note:* CHEMBL213 is the canonical EGFR ligand-target id; at run time the exact accession and active-set size must be re-verified against the pinned ChEMBL release (e.g., ChEMBL 34) and recorded in the run manifest, since I am offline and cannot confirm the live ID. Condition = the dominant scaffold family / pharmacophore of EGFR actives, so "targeted" is concrete and the reference distribution is well defined.

## 3. Generative model
**Primary: autoregressive SMILES Transformer** (small: ~124M params, 12 layers, vocab over SMILES tokens). Rationale: (i) most reproducible and CPU-feasible baseline; (ii) natively supports both reward fine-tuning (training-time) and guided resampling (inference-time); (iii) makes Tier-1 hallucination (unparseable/invalid SMILES) cleanly measurable.
**Secondary (robustness only): a diffusion model (MoleculeDiff-style)** — NOT a full factorial; a single arm, full-feedback, inference-time only (see §5, arm R). This tests whether the effect is model-family-agnostic without inflating scope.

## 4. Chemical-feedback signal and exact reward function
Three signals, all computable on CPU from the SMILES via RDKit + a learned proxy:
- **pLogP** (RDKit MolLogP).
- **QED** (RDKit, classical desirability).
- **Affinity proxy**: a learned QSAR/ML regressor (Gradient-Boosted Trees or small MLP on Mordred + ECF4) trained on ChEMBL pKd/ΔG for EGFR actives. Output converted to an affinity score. *Optional sensitivity check only:* oracle docking (AutoDock Vina against a fixed EGFR crystal structure) — explicitly not a required arm (cost/validity), reported only as a robustness note.

**Reward function (exact):**
r = w₁·f(pLogP) + w₂·QED + w₃·A(affinity)
- **f(pLogP)** = trapezoidal membership over the optimal **band [1, 4]**: f = 1 for 1 ≤ pLogP ≤ 4; linear ramp to 0 over [0,1] and [4,6]; f = 0 outside [0,6]. (A Gaussian centred at 2.5, σ≈1.2 is the alternative; trapezoid is the default for interpretability.) This encodes the bounded-band decision — unbounded logP optimisation is a known reward-hacking failure mode.
- **QED** ∈ [0,1] used directly.
- **A(affinity)** = min-max normalised affinity score to [0,1] (higher = better binding).
- **Default weights: w₁ = w₂ = w₃ = 1/3** (equal). *Sensitivity note:* a one-factor sensitivity run (w ∈ {0.2, 0.5, 0.8} on the dominant term, renormalised) is optional to show the conclusion is not an artefact of equal weighting.

## 5. Arms / control structure
Injection strategies: **(A)** training-time reward-weighted/preference fine-tuning; **(B)** inference-time rejection/guided resampling (keep/re-rank top-k by r); **(C)** both.

| Arm | Feedback properties | Injection | Role |
|-----|--------------------|-----------|------|
| C0 | none | — | Baseline (no feedback) |
| C1 | QED only | A, B | Single-property ablation |
| C2 | pLogP + QED (no affinity) | A, B | Two-property ablation |
| C3 | pLogP + QED + affinity (full) | A, B, C | **Treatment** |
| R | full (C3) | B only, diffusion model | Optional robustness (1 condition) |

So the core factorial is {C0, C1, C2, C3} × {A, B} = 7 trained/configured arms (C0 is a single no-feedback arm), plus C3-C and optional R. C0 is run once and shared.

## 6. Datasets
- **Training set:** EGFR actives from pinned ChEMBL (CHEMBL213) + scaffold-balanced general molecules (ChEMBL-25 / ZINC subset) to avoid overfitting to one class; ~**200k–1M** unique valid molecules after standardisation/dedup.
- **Reference "real-world" distribution:** the **ChEMBL EGFR active set** (CHEMBL213) — this defines "real-world" for all alignment metrics.
- **Leakage control:** strict train/reference split — the reference set used for Fréchet/Tanimoto is **disjoint** from the generator's training molecules (activity-based hold-out or time-split by approval date), to avoid reference-set leakage (see §9).
- **Generation:** scaffold-conditioned, ≥**1,000 molecules per arm** (target 2,000 for stability of distinct-n and chain-length tails).

## 7. Metrics
**Primary:**
- (P1) Mean property scores of *valid* molecules: pLogP (band-hit rate), QED, affinity-proxy pKd/ΔG — vs C0.
- (P2) **Tier-1 hallucination rate** = fraction of outputs that are unparseable SMILES / RDKit-sanitisation failures / infeasible valences.
- (P3) **Distribution alignment** = Fréchet distance on Mordred descriptors to the ChEMBL reference + mean ECF4 Tanimoto to reference set (Fréchet-like).

**Secondary:**
- (S1) **Diversity:** distinct-n (n=1,2,3), scaffold coverage / Bertz index over unique scaffolds, novelty (fraction not in training).
- (S2) **Ultra-long-chain frequency** (contiguous carbon chains >10 C atoms) — reported as a **diversity/distribution metric**, NOT folded into Tier-1 hallucination.
- (S3) **Tier-2 chemical reasonableness** (reported separately): exotic ring systems, multiple disconnected fragments.
- (S4) Oracle-docking affinity (optional sensitivity arm only).

Note on the research question's mapping: "reduces molecular hallucinations" → **Tier 1 (P2)**; "preserving diversity / avoiding ultra-long chains" → **S1 + S2**.

## 8. Statistical analysis plan
- Per metric, compare each feedback arm (C1, C2, C3 under A/B/C) to C0 with a two-sided test: Welch t-test for continuous means (or Mann–Whitney U if non-normal), and two-proportion z-test for hallucination/chain rates.
- **Bonferroni correction** across the 4 primary comparisons (P1-QED, P1-affinity, P2, P3) at family-wise α = 0.05.
- Diversity **non-inferiority** test for C3 vs C0 (margin 10% relative) to confirm no mode collapse.
- Precompute all arms from the same seed set of conditioning scaffolds; report 95% CIs via bootstrapping (≥1000 resamples). Multiple-seed (3 seeds) average to control for training stochasticity.

## 9. Risk-and-mitigation table
| Risk | Mechanism | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|------------|
| Reward hacking via logP | Model inflates/deflates logP to game the band | Bounded trapezoid band [1,4]; band-hit-rate reported separately from raw pLogP; cap extreme values (f=0 outside [0,6]) |
| Mode collapse under RL fine-tuning | Training-time reward narrows output distribution | Monitor distinct-n / scaffold coverage as guardrails; non-inferiority test; compare A vs B to isolate collapse to training-time; keep exploration (temperature/top-p) during fine-tuning |
| Reference-set leakage | Train ∩ reference overlap inflates alignment | Strict disjoint activity/time split; assert zero overlap in run manifest |
| Affinity proxy bias | Learned QSAR mis-scores novel scaffolds | Report proxy AUC on hold-out; optional oracle-docking sensitivity arm; treat affinity as one of three equal-weighted terms |
| Ultra-long-chain exploitation | Model finds a chain-length loophole to raise a score | Explicit S2 metric; no chain term in reward, so any chain growth is flagged as diversity drift |
| Reward-weight sensitivity | Equal weights may be arbitrary | Optional one-factor weight sensitivity run (§4) |

## 10. Feasibility
- **Descriptor set:** Mordred (~1,800 descriptors, NaN-imputed) + **ECFP4 1024-bit** fingerprints, all precomputed with RDKit on CPU.
- **Training set size:** ~200k–1M molecules (EGFR actives + scaffold-balanced general set).
- **Per-arm generation:** ≥1,000 molecules (target 2,000).
- **Compute:** small SMILES Transformer (~124M params) trains on CPU in hours; 3 seeds × 7 arms of fine-tuning/resampling and ≥7k generations are tractable on the 224-CPU allocation. Affinity regressor (GBM/MLP) trains in minutes.
- **Wall-clock estimate:** ~**1–3 days** end-to-end (precompute descriptors + train proxy ~0.5 day; train 3 seeds ~1 day; generation + metric computation ~0.5–1 day), comfortably within a CPU-only, design-and-run budget. All steps reproducible from a pinned ChEMBL release + fixed seeds.

## 11. Assumptions (separate from fixed requirements)
- "Real-world" = ChEMBL EGFR active set (a judgment call; alternatives: ZINC purchasable, broad ChEMBL).
- Tier-1 hallucination = structural validity only; ultra-long chains are a diversity metric (per researcher confirmation).
- Affinity = learned QSAR proxy as primary; oracle docking optional only (per confirmation).
- pLogP = bounded optimal band [1,4] (per confirmation); equal reward weights as default.
- Target = EGFR (CHEMBL213) chosen from the researcher's allowed set; exact ChEMBL accession to be re-verified offline-unavailable at run time.

## 12. What constitutes a positive / null / negative answer
**Positive:** The full-feedback arm (C3) meets the pre-registered criterion — Fréchet distance to the ChEMBL reference drops ≥10% **and** mean QED rises ≥0.05 **and** affinity improves, all p<0.05 Bonferroni-corrected, **with** scaffold coverage and distinct-3 losing <10% (no mode collapse) **and** Tier-1 hallucination not increasing — and the effect persists across injection modes and, if run, the diffusion robustness arm. This supports the claim that the feedback loop improves quality, reduces hallucinations, aligns with real-world distributions, and preserves diversity.
**Null:** Property scores and alignment are statistically unchanged from C0 (confidence intervals cross the pre-registered margins) — the feedback loop has no material effect; the mechanism is inconclusive.
**Negative:** Feedback raises property scores **but** at the cost of significantly reduced diversity (mode collapse, distinct-3/scaffold coverage drop ≥10%) **or** increased Tier-1 hallucination **or** increased ultra-long-chain frequency — i.e., the loop "works" on the reward but fails the alignment-and-diversity-preservation portion of the research question, indicating reward-driven over-optimisation rather than genuine improvement.
